subject: Uptime bridge + fallback fee — clarification on pricing and packaging
messages:
From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>
To: Elena Morris <elena@brightpeak.io>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>, Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 01 May 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Uptime bridge + fallback fee — clarification on pricing and packaging

Elena — thanks for taking the time yesterday. Per our call, I wanted to capture the two items you asked us to confirm: 1) the temporary "uptime bridge" that covers the migration window while you onboard to Dedicated capacity, and 2) the proposed fallback fee model if traffic unexpectedly falls back to the hosted SLA.

High-level proposal (attached in the PDF):
- Uptime bridge: 99.9% target for the 60-day migration window, priced as a one-time bridging fee that nets into year-one committed TCV if you convert to Dedicated within 90 days.
- Fallback fee: nominal per-hour/incident fee when requests are routed to the hosted pool because of capacity constraints or cross-region failover. This is designed to compensate priority routing and avoid surprise bill shock, not to act as a penalty.

Questions we want your feedback on:
- Does the bridge need to cover multiple regions or just us-west?
- Would you prefer the fallback fee capped monthly or per-incident?

Kimberly, Jordan — looping you in to confirm the numbers in the attached and any constraints on mixing commit discounts with bridge credits.

Thanks,
Marcus
Marcus Lin
Head of Sales, Redwood Inference
marcus_lin@redwood.ai
Redwood Inference

Attachment: BPX-SLO-Proposal-20270501.pdf (proposal, 6 pages)

From: Elena Morris <elena@brightpeak.io>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>, Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 03 May 2027 08:27:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Uptime bridge + fallback fee — clarification on pricing and packaging

Marcus — thanks for the summary. A few clarifying notes from BrightPeak's side: 

1) Regions: we'll be migrating our primary production workload to us-west, but we run a DR replica in eu-west that may receive traffic during failover tests. The bridge should cover both (us-west primary + eu-west DR) if possible.

2) Fallback fee model: we prefer a monthly cap rather than per-incident billing — ops teams dislike lots of small charges. Would a capped monthly fallback fee (with a clear threshold for free fallback minutes per month) work?

3) Commit conversion: the team is comfortable with bridge fees becoming credits against year-one Dedicated commit if we convert, but we'd like a clear timeline and a written example of how credits amortize against monthly invoices.

Can you also confirm whether the fallback fee includes priority queueing when we hit the hosted pool? That was a bit ambiguous on the call.

Thanks — Elena
Elena Morris
VP of Platform Engineering, BrightPeak Analytics
elena@brightpeak.io

On Sat, May 1, 2027 at 9:12 AM Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai> wrote:
> Elena — thanks for taking the time yesterday. Per our call, I wanted to capture the two items you asked us to confirm: 1) the temporary "uptime bridge" ...

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>
To: Elena Morris <elena@brightpeak.io>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>
Cc: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 03 May 2027 11:03:00 -07:00
Subject: RE: Uptime bridge + fallback fee — clarification on pricing and packaging

Elena — appreciated. A few specifics to address your points and give you an example amortization: 

1) Region coverage: we can include both us-west and eu-west in the 60-day bridge. The bridge fee scales with the number of regions covered; I've attached a worksheet with 1-region and 2-region pricing lines (BrightPeak-MAP-worksheet.xlsx).

2) Fallback fee design: proposed structure:
   - Free fallback: first 120 minutes of hosted fallback per month (across both regions) at no charge.
   - Capped fallback: subsequent usage billed at $45/hour up to a monthly cap of $6,000.
   - If customer converts to a Dedicated commit before day 90, bridge fee (100% of what you paid) converts to a pre-paid credit that amortizes daily against the first 90 days of Dedicated invoices. Example in worksheet shows $30k bridge -> $333/day credit.

3) Priority queueing: yes — the fallback fee includes priority routing (fast-path) for those requests while you're on the hosted pool. We will explicitly document the priority tiers and expected p95 latency delta in the SLA addendum.

Notes and limits:
- Bridge credits cannot be combined with other promotional credits.
- If fallback usage is sustained above threshold for 3 consecutive months, we'll recommend migrating early and can discuss a temporary discount on commit levels to ease the transition.

I've attached both the proposal PDF and the worksheet. Happy to hop on a 30-minute call to walk through the amortization numbers.

Best,
Kimberly Park
Director, Commercial Pricing, Redwood Inference
kimberly_park@redwood.ai

Attachments: BPX-SLO-Proposal-20270501.pdf, BrightPeak-MAP-worksheet.xlsx

> On Mon, May 3, 2027 at 08:27 AM Elena Morris <elena@brightpeak.io> wrote:
> > Marcus — thanks for the summary. A few clarifying notes from BrightPeak's side: ...

From: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.ai>
To: Elena Morris <elena@brightpeak.io>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 03 May 2027 15:47:00 -07:00
Subject: RE: Uptime bridge + fallback fee — clarification on pricing and packaging

Elena — quick counter-proposal to simplify ops and billing: 

Option A (preferred by BrightPeak ops per your note): Monthly capped fallback with free minutes (as Kimberly outlined). We'll set a clear alert threshold so your SREs know when fallback minutes are being consumed.

Option B (discounted bridge + usage-based fallback): Reduce the 60-day bridge by 15% if you accept per-incident fallback billing ($50/hr, no monthly cap). This lowers upfront TCV but transfers more variability to usage.

Operational ask: If you pick Option A, we need a short addendum signed that lists the regional coverage and the monthly fallback cap so billing doesn't auto-escalate. I'll prepare a 1-page amendment and circulate for signature.

Next steps suggestion: Elena, if you can confirm region coverage (1 or 2) and preferred Option (A vs B) by EOD Friday, we will: 1) send the 1-page addendum, 2) schedule a 30-minute walk-through with your SREs on Tuesday to review priority queueing and alerting, and 3) lock the bridge invoice to convert to credits on commit conversion.

I'll add language to clarify that bridge credits rank ahead of promotional credits but behind committed billing credits in the invoice waterfall.

Thanks — Jordan
Jordan Blake
Enterprise Sales, Redwood Inference
jordan_blake@redwood.ai
